opportunities.title: Coldcard's $247M Month: 15 Attackers, One Laundering Trail, and 210,000 BTC That Should Never Have Moved
opportunities.why_now: The Coldcard exploit has snowballed from a single incident into July's second-worst loss month, with attacker count, mixer flows, and mass wallet migrations all confirmed within 48 hours of each other.
opportunities.angle: Timeline explainer stitching together the Galaxy attacker count, the mixer transfer, and the on-chain wallet exodus into one 'anatomy of a hardware wallet failure' piece — end with the operational lesson for anyone still holding a Coldcard-era seed.

opportunities.title: Bitcoin ETFs Got a Hack Bump. Nobody Can Explain Why. That's the Whole Point.
opportunities.why_now: A Bloomberg analyst is publicly puzzled that ETF inflows rose right after a major custody hack, which is exactly the kind of 'market shrugs at security' moment this channel exists to call out.
opportunities.angle: Contrarian markets-meets-security take: institutional capital doesn't price custody risk the way self-custodied users do — use it to reframe what 'already priced in' actually means for ETF buyers vs. wallet holders.

opportunities.title: No, Your Ledger Isn't a Coldcard — But Here's the Question the Headline Is Dodging
opportunities.why_now: Cointelegraph's own magazine piece is asking whether all hardware wallets are now insecure, which is the exact panic-vs-substance question our audience wants answered without the hedging.
opportunities.angle: Direct rebuttal/explainer format: separate the Coldcard-specific firmware/supply-chain failure from generic hardware wallet risk, then give a concrete checklist for what actually needs verifying on any device.

opportunities.title: France Is Now a Wrench-Attack Hotspot — Your Threat Model Needs a Physical Layer
opportunities.why_now: Chainalysis just quantified $30M in violent crypto extraction attacks in 2026 with France emerging as the epicenter, a data point that's rarely covered with real numbers attached.
opportunities.angle: Security-ops piece translating the Chainalysis research into practical opsec: visible wealth signals, multisig/duress wallets, and why 'not your keys' physical exposure matters as much as custody risk.

opportunities.title: MetaMask's New 'Autonomous' AI Wallet Is an Attack Surface With a Marketing Budget
opportunities.why_now: MetaMask just shipped a self-custodial AI wallet for autonomous trading in the same week Meta and OpenAI both disclosed AI agents independently coordinating hacks — the timing is too good to ignore.
opportunities.angle: Skeptical first-look piece: walk through what 'autonomous crypto trading' actually means for key exposure and agent permissions, tying it to the same-week AI-agent-hacking disclosures for a 'this is what's coming' warning.
